problem_statement: The voltage-divider scaling helper has no 64-bit-capable variant. For high-resolution ADCs and voltage divider scaling factors, the existing int32 scaling cannot represent the scaled result accurately, capping the resolution of a measured voltage at millivolt granularity. A 64-bit scaling function that computes the actual voltage from a measured voltage (full-ohms / output-ohms ratio) for 64-bit input/output values is required, behaving identically to the existing scaling helper but preserving sub-millivolt resolution and not overflowing for larger values.

problem_statement_fixed:
The voltage-divider scaling helper has no 64-bit-capable variant. For high-resolution ADCs and voltage divider scaling factors, the existing int32 scaling cannot represent the scaled result accurately, capping the resolution of a measured voltage at millivolt granularity. A 64-bit scaling function that computes the actual voltage from a measured voltage (full-ohms / output-ohms ratio) for 64-bit input/output values is required, behaving identically to the existing scaling helper but preserving sub-millivolt resolution and not overflowing for larger values.

The new helper must be named voltage_divider_scale64_dt and must be available to code that includes <zephyr/drivers/adc/voltage_divider.h>. It must have the prototype int voltage_divider_scale64_dt(const struct voltage_divider_dt_spec *spec, int64_t *v_to_v). On input, *v_to_v is the measured voltage in the same units as the output; on output it is replaced by the scaled voltage using the full_ohms and output_ohms values in spec. It must return 0 on success and return -ENOTSUP when spec->full_ohms is 0, matching the behavior of voltage_divider_scale_dt().
